audit.whatIsWrong: The entire page is built around respecting Wind Wall — it is in tldr, focus.text, whys[3], wants.you[1], wants.foe[1], spikes[2], spikes[3], mid and late. Wind Wall does nothing to Garen.
audit.why: Riot's Wind Wall text: 'Creates a moving wall that blocks all enemy projectiles.' Garen's kit contains no projectile: Decisive Strike is an empowered melee attack at 300 range, Courage is self-cast, Judgment is a 325-range spin around him, and Demacian Justice is a 400-range targeted execute. Not one carries the projectile flag in the kit file. So the wall he is holding for your commit cannot block a single thing you cast, and every 'wait for Wind Wall' line is telling the player to waste his own strongest window. His real answers are Sweeping Blade — which is a 0.5s-cooldown dash but cannot be re-cast on the same enemy for a few seconds, so he needs minions to escape a spin — and the two-stack Steel Tempest knockup.
audit.corrected: State plainly that Wind Wall blocks projectiles and Garen has none, and re-point the fear at Sweeping Blade's minion jumps and the Steel Tempest knockup.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three chart rows are wrong on both layers. Packet is Garen, Garen, Garen, Garen, Garen, Yasuo, Yasuo; the pages read Garen, Skill, Garen, Garen, Skill, Garen, Yasuo.
audit.why: whys[1] says 'Yasuo stays flimsy at level 2 while your Q-silence and autos out-trade him' (Garen, not Skill); whys[4] says 'Demacian Justice at 6 executes a diving Yasuo through his passive shield' (Garen, not Skill); whys[5] says 'His first crit item and Steel Tempest poke begin out-damaging your spins' (Yasuo, not Garen). The 55.22% win rate over 6994 games backs a strongly Garen-favoured early game.
audit.corrected: Level 2 -> Garen 6/10; Level 6 -> Garen 6/10; First item -> Yasuo 4/10. Rows 1, 3, 4-5 and 2+ items already match.

audit.whatIsWrong: report[5] gives Last Breath as 80s and describes it as 'his all-in after a knockup' without saying where the knockup comes from.
audit.why: Last Breath is 70/50/30 — 70s at rank 1, and only 30s at rank 3, which is the real reason the late game inverts. It blinks to an Airborne enemy champion, so it requires a knockup first. Garen has no knockup in his kit, so the only setup in a 1v1 is Yasuo's own two-stack Steel Tempest whirlwind — which means denying that second stack denies the ultimate entirely.
audit.corrected: Quote 70s at rank 1 and 30s at rank 3, and name the two-stack Steel Tempest as the only 1v1 setup.

notes: HIGHEST-VALUE FINDING OF MY SLICE: this page told Garen players to wait out Wind Wall before committing. Wind Wall blocks projectiles; Garen's kit has no projectile in any slot (verified against ownerKit flags — Q is an empowered melee attack, E is a self-centred spin, R is targeted). Holding your all-in for a wall that cannot touch you is a pure loss of tempo in a 55% win-rate lane. I corrected every line I could reach inside the length band.
